channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed

item.title: Trump Energy Boss Says Fuel Export Ban Wouldn’t Cut Fuel Prices
item.description: One of President Donald Trump’s top energy chiefs said a US ban on fuel exports or crude wouldn’t bring down pump prices.
item.dc:creator: Ari Natter

item.title: Cook Says Saudi Arabia Is in a ‘Vulnerable’ Position
item.description: Steven Cook, senior fellow for Middle East and Africa studies at the Council on Foreign Relations, says Saudi Arabia made a “grave miscalculation” in confronting the Houthis and now finds itself in an “extraordinarily strategically vulnerable position.” Cook says the situation gives Iran another source of leverage, raises questions about US reliability as a regional security partner, and could contribute to a continued rise in diesel and other refined product prices if no agreement is reached over passage through the Strait of Hormuz. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Holtz-Eakin Says No Rate Hike Would Undercut Fed Credibility
item.description: Douglas Holtz-Eakin, President of the American Action Forum and former Director of the Congressional Budget Office, says the Federal Reserve should raise interest rates this week and warns that failing to do so would undercut its credibility as inflation remains its central challenge. He also calls President Donald Trump’s proposed $5,000 dividend checks an “unthinkably large” stimulus that could force the Fed’s hand, arguing that Washington has shown little fiscal discipline as borrowing costs rise and the government moves closer to borrowing simply to cover interest on previous debt. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Global AI Supercycle (Podcast)
item.description:
AI developers including Anthropic and OpenAI are clashing with the Trump administration over their calls for an industrywide slowdown in artificial intelligence development, a proposal that’s already triggered a selloff across technology stocks and has brought into question the resilience of a global data center boom. Bloomberg Economics uses a state-of-the-art approach to estimate exposure to AI across major economies, and expertise from the US and UK to Mainland China, South Korea, Taiwan and beyond to assess the current impact and future outlook.
On today's episode:
Tom Orlik, Bloomberg Economics Chief Economist Mike Shepard, Bloomberg News Senior Editor of Technology & Strategic Industries Brian Moynihan, Bank of America CEO with Bloomberg Deals Host, Dani Burger John Tozzi, Bloomberg News Health Care Reporter (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Mitch McConnell Returns to Senate for First Time Since June
item.description: Republican Senator Mitch McConnell returned to the US Senate on Monday for the first time since suffering from a fall at his home on June 14.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson

item.title: Newsom Says He Won’t Run for President If Kamala Harris Does
item.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom said he would not run for president in 2028 if former Vice President Kamala Harris enters the race, ruling out a potential primary showdown between two of California’s most prominent Democrats.
item.dc:creator: Alicia Clanton

item.title: As Tensions with US Rise, Mark Carney Looks To Europe
item.description: In the midst of a trade war with the US, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is on a charm offensive. On today’s Big Take podcast, Bloomberg’s Derek Decloet and host David Gura break down how Canada is reassessing its trade and security relationships and cozying up to Europe. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: David Sacks: Anthropic, OpenAI Should Slow AI If Deemed Necessary
item.description: David Sacks, chair of the President's Council of Advisors on Science & Technology, says Anthropic and OpenAI should slow development of their most advanced AI models if they believe the technology poses serious risks, but argues they don’t need new regulation to do it. He pushes back against calls for antitrust exemptions and a broader regulatory framework, saying today’s frontier AI labs are setting the frontier themselves and do not need "anyone else's permission." He also underlines that any approach must account for competition with China, which is unlikely to join a global agreement to slow down AI development. He speaks to Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia CEO Puts Trump on Phone While Downplaying AI Risks
item.description: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang took a live phone call from Donald Trump during a panel discussion Monday, allowing the US president to dismiss artificial intelligence dangers as a “hoax.”
item.dc:creator: Ian King

item.title: Trump Remains Bullish on AI, Even as White House Debates Regulation and Risk
item.description: An economic engine could became a major political liability
item.dc:creator: Nancy Cook

item.title: AI Bosses Urge Caution, Bonds Climb
item.description: AI developers including Anthropic and OpenAI are clashing with the Trump administration over their calls for an industrywide slowdown in AI development. Bloomberg News Senior Editor of Technology & Strategic Industries Mike Shepard explains the increasing tensions. It comes as President Trump continues to clash with Canada's Mark Carney. Bloomberg News Executive Editor for Canada Derek Decloet breaks down the latest news. Then, Vertical Aerospace CEO Stuart Simpson talks about growing the eclectic aviation industry to become more commercialized. Plus, Bloomberg's Mike Mckee breaks down why the 10-year yield is breaching 5% and what is means for the FOMC meeting this week. Finally, Bloomberg's Dani Burger interviews Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan as shares drop on news that trading revenue will be "relatively flat" in the third quarter compared to last year. All on the latest episode of "Bloomberg Businessweek Daily. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Challenges AI Guardrails
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Kailey Leinz discusses the calls to rein in advanced artificial intelligence models. On today's show, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Bully Pulpit International Managing Partner Adam Hodge and Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget President Maya MacGuineas. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Crypto Bill Text Released Ahead of Senate Vote
item.description: Bloomberg's Tyler Kendall broke down the potential sticking points around the Clarity Act after Senate Republicans released updated text of the bill in anticipation of a vote this week. The text includes an updated ethics provision that was a main roadblock to get Democrats on board, that would give state attorneys general some authority rules and will push elected officials to put their digital asset holdings into a blind trust or forced divestiture. The bill also faces pushback from community banks concerned about deposit flight. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Dividend Would Come With 'Doozy' of a Price Tag, Says Maya MacGuineas
item.description: Maya MacGuineas, president of the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget, on Trump’s proposal, to give $5,000 checks to adult Americans carries a `doozy' of a price tag. MacGuineas said that the president is governing with 'Oprah politics' of making fiscal promises and is concerned that both parties will fall onto a 'wagon of competing promises' to try and win over voters ahead of the midterms. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Texas Republican Slammed for Racist Post About Longhorn Fans
item.description: As Texas Longhorns football fans basked in their comeback win over top-ranked Ohio State this weekend, a photograph of gleeful students ignited a fresh round of Republican infighting over immigration and assimilation — just as the party is seeking unity ahead of the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Joe Lovinger

item.title: House Speaker Risks Trump Ire, Signals Openness to AI Guardrails
item.description: House Speaker Mike Johnson is showing an openness to regulation of artificial intelligence that clashes with President Donald Trump’s clear hostility to the idea, creating a divide within the party just weeks before a midterm election where Republicans are already facing strong headwinds.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson

item.title: The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations Celebrates 10 Years
item.description: For a decade, David Rubenstein has sat down with some of the biggest names in business, finance, politics and culture. We look back at 10 of the most memorable moments from "The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DOJ Covid Loan-Fraud Crackdown Finds $245 Million in Losses
item.description: The US Justice Department said a federal crackdown by prosecutors this summer uncovered hundreds of millions of dollars in fraud tied to Covid-relief programs, resulting in criminal charges against dozens of defendants.
item.dc:creator: Chris Strohm and Jimmy Jenkins

item.title: Trump Claims Russia-Ukraine Energy Truce; Kyiv Says Not Yet
item.description: President Donald Trump and Ukraine offered differing accounts of a supposed agreement with Russia to stop attacks on energy infrastructure, as strikes on oil refineries help drive diesel prices to record levels.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron and Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: Carney Calls for Global AI Oversight Body to Ensure Safe Development
item.description: Canada wants to see the creation of a global “technology stability” body to help oversee artificial intelligence and ensure it is safe, Prime Minister Mark Carney said.
item.dc:creator: Brian Platt and Christine Dobby
